chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abū Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn 'Alī al-Washshā', from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام saying: When a man dies among women, his wife washes him. If his wife is not with him, then the one among them who is most entitled to him washes him, and she wraps a cloth over her hands, and there is no objection in that.

key_terms.أَوْلَاهُنَّ بِهِ: the one among them most closely entitled or related to him
key_terms.خِرْقَةً: a piece of cloth used as a covering
key_terms.غَسَّلَتْهُ: she washed him ritually after death
key_terms.لَا يُنَافِي: there is no objection or contradiction

ai.seo_question: Who may perform the ghusl of a deceased man if only women are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the ghusl of a deceased man when he is among women. It states that his wife may wash him, and if she is absent, the woman most closely entitled to him may do so while covering her hands with a cloth.
